title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In this 'quatrième mouture' of Analysis situs, Grothendieck builds a purely combinatorial model of a (piecewise-linear, one-dimensional) 'tame' space from a finite ordered set L. The model is a set M whose elements are points P_a (a in L) and segments S_{a,b} (a<b covering). On M he has a relation X |o| Y ('orthogonality' or 'anti-influence'), two operators s-supp° (support) and cos-supp° (co-support) on subsets of M, and the 'ombre' (shadow) Omb(X) of an element. The previous page proves, for a totally ordered L, two things: Cor. 1, s-supp°(P_a) = {P_a}; Cor. 2, the analogous statement for S_{a,b}. In effect, for a chain the support of a point or segment is that point or segment, and Lemma 1 gives Omb(X) = s-supp(X~).

Top of this page: 'Ceci ne se fait pas [sans] l'hyp[othèse]', followed by a counterexample. Take L = {a, c < b}, the 'Λ' poset with a→b and c→b. Then M = {P_a, P_b, P_c, S_ab, S_cb}, so card M = 5, as noted.
- He computes cos-supp°(P_b) = M \ {P_b} and cos-supp°({P_a}) = {P_b, S_ab, S_cb} (as best I can read it).
- s-supp°({P_a}) = {P_a, P_c} (the subscript is overwritten), which is ≠ {P_a}. So Cor. 1 fails without linearity: the two minimal elements a and c cannot be separated by |o|.
- cos-supp°(S_ab~) = ∅ and s-supp°(S_ab~) = M ≠ Omb(S_ab). Here Omb(S_ab) = {P_a, P_b, S_ab}, and the NB records M = Omb(S_ab) ⊔ {S_cb, P_c}. So Lemma 1 also fails: the 'shadow' of a segment is no longer its support once the order branches.

He then starts a second counterexample on the diamond poset c<a<b, c<d<b (a cycle, i.e. a circle) and abandons it. He also crosses out a 'Lemma 2', which reads: if X ∥ Y (parallel or independent), Φ ⊂ Omb(X) = s-supp(X~) and Ψ ⊂ Omb(Y), then s-supp°(Φ∪Ψ) = s-supp°Φ ∪ s-supp°Ψ. This is additivity of the support for 'separated' pieces.

4 July, new section: 'Détermination des polygones, ou ensembles constructibles dans M'. For the reduced order relation, a polygon (a constructible subset of M) splits into connected components, which are connected polygons. He begins listing the types of components (dim 0: a closed point {P_a}; dim 1: 'figures') and crosses the list out. The next page completes it. Convex pre-figures are classified by pairs (T, α): T is a flag (chain) in L, and α is a subset of the boundary ∂T = {min T, max T} that is removed. This yields closed, half-open and open segments.

In modern terms: constructible subsets of a finite 1-dimensional cell complex (the Hasse diagram of L) decompose into connected pieces. Each convex piece is a chain-indexed cell with an arbitrary subset of its two endpoints removed. This is the standard combinatorial description of constructible (semi-linear, o-minimal-definable) subsets of a graph, phrased via an order relation and Alexandrov-type supports.
errors: The opening lines are hard to read; 'Ceci ne se fait pas [sans] l'hyp.' is my reconstruction, not a certain reading.

The braces in 'cos-supp°({P_a}) = {P_b}, S_ab, S_cb' are misplaced. The intended set is presumably {P_b, S_ab, S_cb} (or a subset of it); whether S_ab belongs to the co-support of P_a depends on definitions not visible on this page.
The overwritten subscript in s-supp°({P_a}) = {P_a, P_?} should be P_c. Only then is the claimed inequality ≠ {P_a} the counterexample to Cor. 1.
Lemma 2 is crossed out without proof, probably because the counterexamples show s-supp° is not well-behaved outside the linear case. No mathematical error is visible in what remains.

ideas.what: Counterexample showing that support = point (s-supp°(P_a) = {P_a}) and shadow = support of segment fail for a non-linearly ordered (branching) L
ideas.modern_name: Failure of separation and locality properties in Alexandrov / specialization-order models of branching graphs

ideas.what: Additivity of support over 'parallel' (independent) pieces (crossed-out Lemma 2)
ideas.modern_name: additivity of supports / closure over separated sets

ideas.what: Classification of constructible subsets ('polygones') of the combinatorial model M: decomposition into connected components; convex pieces indexed by a flag T plus a subset of its endpoints (closed, half-open, open segments)
ideas.modern_name: cell decomposition of definable/semilinear sets in dimension 1; constructible sets of a finite poset / order complex
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality cell decomposition (van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn 1984–86); semilinear geometry
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 only programmatically announces tame topology and 'dévissage' of stratified structures; this combinatorial classification is not there

missed.claim: This page documents the 1986 'Analysis situs' attempt to axiomatize tame topology combinatorially via orders, supports, co-supports and 'ombres'. It records the specific test that branching posets break the support/shadow lemmas. This thread of Grothendieck's tame-topology programme is essentially unknown in the literature. Mathematically it is elementary and parallels o-minimal cell decomposition.
missed.quote: Détermination des polygones, ou ensembles constructibles dans M.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of historical interest: it shows Grothendieck developing a 'tame topology' foundation independently of the o-minimality school, at the same time (1984–86). No new theorem for specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine counterexamples and the start of an elementary classification of 1-dimensional constructible sets. Historically interesting as part of the unpublished tame-topology effort, but mathematically standard.
transcription_corrections: Top-left margin word is likely 'Contre-ex.' (underlined), consistent with the transcription.
In 's-supp°({P_a}) = {P_a, P_c}' the second element is overwritten and should be read as P_c (the transcription has the argument as {P_b}).
The first formula under the diagram reads 'f = cos-supp°(P_b) = M \ {P_b}' or similar, with the leading symbol unclear.
Lemma 2 begins 'Soient X, Y ⊂ M avec X ∥ Y' after crossing out 'Φ ⊂ M, Ψ ⊂ M'; the whole lemma is struck through.
